solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Time to leave port, having forged eighth hidden identity?

indicators.note: hidden says one piece is tucked away inside the other
forged means faked or hammered into a new shape, so the letters of eighth are reworked

parts.note: ID is the usual short form of identity, as on an ID card

explanation.surface: A spy forging papers assumes a secret eighth identity before slipping out of harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time to leave port' is the definition: ships sail when the water is deepest. 'forged' is the anagram signal and 'hidden' the container signal, not part of the spy story.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships traditionally sail on the high tide, when the water is deepest in the harbour.

clue.text: Retail customer ignoring South American painter

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so the letter for South is dropped from the customer

parts.note: a shopper is a customer in a shop
S is the compass abbreviation for South

explanation.surface: A shop customer snubs a painter from South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' reads as one phrase, but South is the S to drop and American belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Hopper was the US artist famous for Nighthawks and lonely urban scenes.

clue.text: Spin around Germany on vacation — give the thumbs up

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied out, so only the outside letters of Germany remain

parts.note: to rate something is to judge it favourably, as with a thumbs-up

explanation.surface: A tourist spinning round Germany on holiday gives the trip a thumbs up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties Germany to GY.
explanation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to whirl or rotate about a centre, a synonym of spin around.

clue.text: Took LSD — in an excited state fell over

parts.note: to trip is slang for being high on LSD, so took LSD gives tripped
up means excited or lively, as in all worked up

explanation.surface: Someone high on acid gets overexcited and falls down.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripped up is a phrasal verb for stumbled and fell, as over a kerb.

clue.text: Held by frayed rope, very thin…guys — stop what you're doing!

indicators.note: held by means the answer is gripped inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A tent held up by thin, frayed guy ropes prompts an urgent call to halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held by' finds the answer running through fraYED ROPE VERY THIN Guys; guys look like people being addressed but are tent ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: Drop everything is an idiom ordering someone to abandon their current task at once.

clue.text: Published, and gets taken to court

definitions.meaning: put out or published, like a book or a statement
read as ..., someone who ... is taken to court

explanation.surface: A writer's book comes out and the author is promptly sued.
explanation.definitionFit: Issued means released to the public; split in two it means faces a lawsuit.

clue.text: Returning US vessel has 25% off fare from Japan

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters of US are read in the opposite order
off means taken away, as in a discount, so a portion of the vessel is removed

parts.note: a ship is a sea-going vessel
a quarter of a four-letter word is one letter, here the final one

explanation.surface: An American ship heading home gets a discount on Japanese food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' gives SU; '25% off' cuts one letter in four from the vessel, a quarter-off discount disguised as maths.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is the Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish, a classic Japanese food.

clue.text: Have Paul round (which means disruption)

indicators.note: round means turned about, so these letters are spun into a new order

explanation.surface: Inviting Paul over causes chaos at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like 'come round to visit' but rearranges HAVE PAUL.
explanation.definitionFit: An upheaval is a sudden violent change or upset, so it amounts to disruption.

clue.text: Papa enters — wiped, drained

indicators.note: enters means goes inside, so the letter for Papa is placed within the other word

parts.note: deleted means wiped, as files from a disk
Papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Dad comes home exhausted and wiped out.
explanation.definitionFit: Depleted means used up or emptied, as with drained resources or energy.

clue.text: Wicked Amir recognised Mafia group

indicators.note: wicked suggests something twisted or bent, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Amir spots a wicked gang of mobsters.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder has an S, so the anagram gives the British spelling ORGANISED, which the grid prints with a Z.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mafia is the classic example of a criminal syndicate, the core of organised crime.

clue.text: Colonnade in Portuguese city, almost freezing!

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the city name

parts.note: Porto is the second city of Portugal, home of port wine

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: icy means freezing cold

explanation.surface: A traveller shelters under a colonnade in a bitterly cold Porto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like it places the colonnade in the city, but it signals the container; 'almost' drops the final letter of the cold word.
explanation.definitionFit: A portico is a porch whose roof rests on columns, so it is a kind of colonnade.

clue.text: Part of thorny plant making stocking tear according to Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, so the first letters are exchanged

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings or tights
a rip is a tear, as in a ladder in tights

explanation.surface: Snagging a stocking on a thorny plant tears it.
explanation.walkthrough: HOSE RIP becomes ROSE HIP when the first letters are swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosehip is the fruit of the rose, which grows on the thorny rose bush.

clue.text: Bar established work

parts.note: est. is the abbreviation for established, as on shop signs
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A long-established pub does its work.
explanation.definitionFit: Estop is a legal term meaning to bar or preclude someone from asserting something.

clue.text: Take out scatty cat, dearie

indicators.note: scatty means scatterbrained and muddled, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone tells a dear friend to remove the dizzy cat.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to destroy completely, and take out is slang for eliminating.

clue.text: It's clear it'll be needed when wrapping Xmas presents

definitions.text: It's clear it'll be needed when wrapping Xmas presents

parts.words: It's clear it'll be needed when wrapping Xmas presents
parts.note: clear reads as obviously, but it describes transparent sticky tape used to seal gift wrap

explanation.surface: Obviously something will be required for Christmas gift wrapping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's clear' sounds like 'obviously' but literally means the item is transparent.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear sticky tape is the standard way to hold wrapping paper closed around a gift.

clue.text: Prevent our agenda being interrupted by camp followers

indicators.note: the answer breaks into these words, so it lies hidden across them

explanation.surface: Someone protests that their plans keep being disrupted by people in a camp.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through prevENT OUR AGEnda.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is a group of attendants who accompany an important person, like camp followers.

clue.text: Adam's garden rubbish piled on top of English anteater

indicators.note: in a down answer, what is piled on top comes first, above the letter for English

parts.note: Adam lived in the Garden of Eden
tat is British slang for cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: Junk from Adam's garden is heaped on an English anteater.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentates are toothless mammals such as anteaters, sloths and armadillos.

clue.text: GOP is now in trouble, dropping suddenly

indicators.note: in trouble suggests something in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Republican Party is now in difficulty, falling sharply in the polls.
explanation.walkthrough: GOP is the Grand Old Party, the US Republicans.
explanation.definitionFit: Swooping is diving down fast, like a bird of prey dropping suddenly.

clue.text: Spent Monday working to secure women's deposits

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so the letter for women is enclosed
working suggests something being worked over, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A spent Monday at work goes on securing women's savings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges SPENT MONDAY, and 'to secure' places W inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Down payments are initial part-payments on a purchase, also called deposits.

clue.text: The endlessly split economy?

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a rift is a split or crack

explanation.surface: A question about an economy that is endlessly divided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts THE to TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrift means careful spending, which is economy in its sense of saving money.

clue.text: Mate…fine day in Paris, nothing in store

indicators.note: in store means kept inside, so the French word is held between the other letters

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
rien is French for nothing

explanation.surface: A friend has a fine day in Paris, with nothing waiting for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Paris' tells you to use French.
explanation.definitionFit: Mate is informal British for a pal or companion, a synonym of friend.

clue.text: Ethnic oil works from the Stone Age

indicators.note: works means operates on, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Traditional oil works date back to prehistoric times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' looks like a noun (factories) but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Neolithic was the later part of the Stone Age, when farming began.

clue.text: Private Victor losing wife

indicators.note: losing means giving up, so the letter for wife is removed

parts.note: the victor is the winner

explanation.surface: A soldier named Victor loses his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private Victor' looks like a soldier's rank and name, but Private is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner thoughts or feelings are private ones, kept within oneself.

clue.text: Escort you, me and that lady

parts.note: you and me together are us
her refers to that lady

explanation.surface: Someone asks to accompany a group including themselves and a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To usher is to show someone to a seat or place, which is to escort them.

clue.text: Old residence of Pontiff which still has a Pont (if short)

definitions.text: Old residence of Pontiff which still has a Pont (if short)

parts.words: Old residence of Pontiff which still has a Pont (if short)
parts.note: the popes lived in this French city in the 14th century, and its famous bridge, the Pont, is broken off midstream; Pont is also Pontiff cut short

explanation.surface: A former papal home still boasts its celebrated, if truncated, bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The French song Sur le pont d'Avignon names the bridge, which now ends partway across the Rhône; 'Pont (if short)' also hides Pontiff less IFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Popes resided in Avignon from 1309 to 1377, so it was a papal residence.

clue.text: International publication censors Arizona picture

indicators.note: censors means cuts out, so the state abbreviation is removed

parts.note: a magazine is a periodical publication
AZ is the postal abbreviation for Arizona

explanation.surface: A global magazine censors a photo of Arizona.
explanation.walkthrough: 'censors' cuts AZ from MAGAZINE, leaving MAGINE.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to form an image of it in the mind, so to imagine it.

clue.text: Wrap a band around Joe, held by nurse and retired doctor

indicators.note: held by means gripped inside, so the soldier goes within the other letters

parts.note: EN is an Enrolled Nurse in Britain

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: GI Joe is the American soldier, so Joe gives GI

explanation.surface: A nurse and a retired doctor hold Joe while wrapping a bandage round him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns DR into RD.
explanation.definitionFit: To engird is to encircle or surround with a girdle, i.e. to put a belt around.

clue.text: Hated exam? Indeed!

indicators.note: In says the exam sits inside the next word

parts.note: taken as written
a test is an exam

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an exam was loathed and is told emphatically yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indeed!' reads as emphatic agreement, but split it into In + deed: the exam goes in a deed.
explanation.definitionFit: Detested means loathed intensely, a stronger synonym of hated.
